ground_truth.description: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.root_cause: In ERC-4337, validateUserOp uses external self-call to isValidSignature, changing msg.sender to wallet instead of entrypoint. BaseAuth.signatureValidation enforces caller binding, causing revert for static signatures bound to entrypoint.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet with static signature bound to entrypoint. Attempt validateUserOp → reverts with InvalidStaticSignatureWrongCaller. PoC: Add test to test/modules/ERC4337v07.t.sol: test_validateUserOp_staticSig_callerMismatch_reverts. Uses server and forge test.
ground_truth.fix_description: Avoid external self-call; propagate intended caller into validation.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The contract is vulnerable to a denial of service (DoS) attack due to the use of an external self-call to `isValidSignature` in `validateUserOp`. Under ERC-4337, `msg.sender` is changed to the wallet instead of the entrypoint, causing a revert when static signatures are bound to the entrypoint.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Deploy a wallet with a static signature bound to the entrypoint. Attempt to call `validateUserOp` to cause a revert due to the static signature validation failure.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Avoid using external self-calls; instead, propagate the intended caller into the validation logic to prevent the change in `msg.sender` from causing a revert.

prediction.overall_explanation: The ERC4337v07 contract is vulnerable to a denial of service attack due to its handling of static signatures in the context of ERC-4337's `validateUserOp` function. The issue arises from the external call to `isValidSignature`, which changes `msg.sender` from the entrypoint to the wallet, causing a revert when static signatures are used. This vulnerability can be mitigated by modifying the validation logic to correctly handle the caller information.
